case_name: Khem Chand v Union of India and Others
facts: On July 1, 1949, the appellant, who was a permanent Sub-Inspector of Co-operative Societies, Delhi, was suspended by the Deputy Commissioner, Delhi; On July 9 he was served with a charge-sheet under r. 6(1) of the Rules which had been framed by the Chief Commissioner, Delhi.
The question arises in this way.
Against this decision of the High Court, the appellant preferred an appeal by special leave to this Court.

On April 20, 1955, i.e., shortly after the Government appeal had been dismissed by the Senior Subordinate judge, the appellant instituted a suit in the Court of the Senior Sub judge, Delhi, out of which the present appeal has arisen.

It is clear that if r. 12(4) of the Central Civil Service (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1957, is valid the appellant must be deemed to have been placed under suspension from December 17, 1951.

The main provisions of Art. 309 is that subject to the provisions of the Constitution, Acts of the appropriate Legislature may regulate the recruitment, and conditions of service of per-sons appointed, to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State.
issues: Whether r. 12(4) of the Central Civil Service (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1957, is valid in law.
Whether the impugned rule contravenes Art. 142, Art. 144, Art. 19(1)(f), Art. 31 and also Art. 14 of the Constitution.
petitioner_arguments: Mr. janardan Sharma rightly contends that this lower of the President to make rules is subject to all the provisions of the Constitution and consequently if in making the rule the rule-making authority has contravened any of the provisions of the Constitution the rule is invalid to the extent of such contravention.
respondent_arguments: The defendants in this suit are: 1. The Union of India; 2. The State of Delhi; and 3. The Collector and Registrar, Co operative Societies, Delhi.
court_reasoning: According to Mr. Sharma r. 12(4) contravenes the provisions of Art. 142, Art. 144, Art. 19(1)(f), Art. 31 and also Art. 14 of the Constitution.
In our judgment, there is no substance in this contention.
holding: The Court held that the impugned rule does not contravene any provision of the Constitution and therefore it is valid.
cases_cited: Khem Chand v Union of India
